correctness.rationale: With s seeds, exactly n-s one-shot edges must transmit, so exactly s-1 unused edges cut the path into s components and each component contains exactly one seed. A retained component is forceable from its unique seed iff its edge times strictly decrease toward the seed from the left and increase away to the right, i.e. iff the block has no strict interior local maximum. Therefore cuts are exactly hitting sets for peak neighborhoods {i-1,i,i+1}. Strict peaks cannot be adjacent; these neighborhoods overlap exactly for peak centers distance two, so each overlap chain of r peaks needs and admits ceil(r/2) cuts. Minimum interval stabbing equals maximum disjoint neighborhoods; their centers lie in 2,...,n-2 and must be at least three apart, giving floor((n-1)/3) extra cuts, achieved by the block timing (1,3,2),(4,6,5),.... The frozen verifier exhausts all timings through n=9 only as a stress test of this all-n proof.

value.rationale: Paths with one-shot injective timings are the canonical minimal connected test family for temporal zero forcing. The theorem gives both an exact per-timing structural formula and the sharp worst timing, converting dynamics into a transparent local-maximum obstruction. This is a natural complete classification rather than a small computational census.

final_claim: For a path whose edges each occur once at pairwise distinct times, temporal zero forcing equals one plus the minimum number of cuts hitting every three-edge neighborhood of a strict local maximum; if peak-overlap chains have lengths r_j, TZ=1+sum ceil(r_j/2), and the worst timing on n vertices has TZ=floor((n+2)/3).
